title: Vendor source systems for the Vla line
purpose: The line PLC (vla-factory) is NOT the only source in a real plant. Every process
part is assembled from vendor skids that each arrive with their own controller,
their own tag names, their own units and their own idea of quality. They are
physically wired to the same product line and informationally wired to nothing.
This file describes those islands: what they are, how you reach them, what they
natively call things, and which canonical ISA-95 tag each native point maps to.
It is deliberately SEPARATE from isa95-vla.json. That file answers 'what is this
equipment and where does it sit in the plant'. This file answers 'how do I reach
it and what does it call things'. Conflating those two is exactly what produced
the four-copies drift that tools/gen-connect.py now prevents.
raw_root_rationale: Raw vendor data lands OUTSIDE the UNS, on its own root, for two reasons.
Anything parked under DairyWorks/ is silently archived to MongoDB. Putting raw
vendor tags there would build a data swamp inside the demo that argues against
2. Rhetorical: in a topic browser the presenter points at two trees. One is a
modelled plant. The other is a junk drawer. That contrast IS the demo.
raw/vla/# is therefore excluded from every archive group and from the TDengine
bridge's MQTT_TOPICS. Unmodelled data is not stored. Model first, then store.
payload_note: There is no single raw payload shape, and that is not sloppiness: each connector
emits its own. MonsterMQ's OPC-UA client publishes {value, timestamp, status},
where 'status' is a numeric OPC-UA StatusCode. The UNS contract is
{value, unit, ts, quality}. They do not line up: different key names, no unit at
all, and a numeric status where the contract wants GOOD/BAD/UNCERTAIN.
So the Condition step is structurally mandatory, not a nice-to-have. You cannot
point a consumer at a raw topic and get something meaningful, no matter how
anonymization: Generic archetypes only. Vendor tokens are vendor-a..vendor-f. No real manufacturer names, model numbers, IP addresses, network paths or vendor schemas anywhere in this file or in anything generated from it (PR-15).
distortion_units_note: Every number inside a 'distortion' block is in the CANONICAL (SI) unit of the
target tag, never in the vendor's unit. So 'offset: 0.8' on a *_C tag is 0.8
degrees CELSIUS, and 'base: 350.0' on a *_L_min tag is 350 litres per minute.
The conversion to the vendor's unit and the scaling to a register integer happen
afterwards, in exactly that order. Mixing the two up produces a value that looks
plausible and is wrong by a factor of 3.8, which is precisely the class of bug

OPC_DA.label: OPC-DA via a DA/UA tunneller
honesty_note: OPC-DA is DCOM and runs on Windows only. It is not implementable in a Linux
container and WE HAVE NOT IMPLEMENTED IT. What we simulate is how you actually
reach a DA island from a Linux data layer: a DA server behind a DA/UA tunneller,
and we connect to the tunneller's OPC-UA endpoint.
The transport is UA; the DATA is DA, and that is the part that matters:
* the DA quality word as a separate companion item (192 GOOD, 64 UNCERTAIN,
* no per-item source timestamp, so the only time you get is receive time
* values as scaled integers, because the underlying registers are integers
Say this out loud in the demo. Claiming a DCOM implementation is exactly the
kind of thing the audience you want to convince will check.

source_systems.description: HTST heat-treatment skid: heats the vla to the hold temperature, holds it, and diverts the flow if the hold tube drops below the legal minimum.
namespace_index_note: Yes, ns=2, the SAME index the line PLC uses for urn:dairyworks. That is not
a clash and not a mistake: namespace indices are per server, not global. Each
server numbers its own namespaces, so the first custom namespace on any server
Which makes the point better than a different number would have: 'ns=2;s=...'
is meaningless on its own. The same string addresses two completely unrelated
things depending on which endpoint you sent it to. A node id without its
endpoint and namespace URI is not an identity, and that is exactly why the
Model step has to mint a stable identity of its own.
the_conflict: This skid and the line PLC measure the same fluid at the same moment, and
they disagree. The vendor RTD sits further down the hold tube, reads about
0.8 C high and lags roughly 2 seconds. Both readings are correct; they are
Run cook_undertemp at magnitude 0.65 and the split becomes a business
decision rather than a rounding argument:
* line PLC   -> peak cook ~76.3 C -> viscosity ~110 cP -> BELOW the 150 cP
spec -> the batch must be held or recooked
* this skid  -> hold tube ~77.1 C, comfortably above the 72 C legal
pasteurisation minimum -> the SAFETY record is clean
So the legal record says the product is safe and the process record says it
is out of spec. Both true. Today nobody sees the second half, because it
lives on an island. That is the entire pitch in one screen.
READ THE DELTA DURING COOKING, NOT DURING A PHASE CHANGE. In steady cooking
the gap is a clean +0.8 C and that is the declared calibration error. At the
COOKING -> COOLING transition it briefly reads tens of degrees high, because
the demo runs at TIME_SCALE 15 and the line drops ~58 C in about one real
second while the island scans at 1 Hz. That spike is a sampling artefact of
the acceleration, not the conflict. Do not put it on a slide.
